title: sprite.ts: depth ordering wrong — li=0 (topmost layer) gets lowest depth
description:
encodeDefineSprite() in packages/swf/src/sprite.ts assigns SWF depths starting from li=0 (the topmost/front layer) upward. This gives li=0 depth=1 (lowest depth = behind everything) instead of the highest depth (= in front). The SWF convention is that higher depth numbers render in front.

compile.ts has a pre-pass (line 1330) that iterates from li=n-1 (background) to li=0 (foreground) so background layers get lower depths and foreground layers get higher depths. sprite.ts has no equivalent pre-pass — it assigns depths in iteration order (li=0 first), which is the reverse of the correct visual order.

Fix: add a depth pre-pass to encodeDefineSprite() that seeds getOrAssignDepth() by iterating from li=layers.length-1 down to li=0, matching compile.ts's approach.
